evidence: The Fear & Greed Index registered a score of 22 ('Extreme Fear') on 2022-11-22, ticking up marginally from 21 on the previous day. Sentiment has been compressed within the Extreme Fear regime (7-day mean of 22.29) following the early November collapse of FTX. While persistent extreme fear reflects severe risk aversion and ongoing structural caution, extended consolidation at deep fear levels often limits fresh aggressive selling pressure in the very near term and produces modest relief bounces. Consequently, the 24-hour directional outlook reflects a slight mean-reverting upward tilt of 51%.
limitations: The Fear & Greed Index reflects trailing aggregate sentiment and volatility rather than real-time order-book flow or immediate breaking news.
Extreme fear conditions during industry-wide solvency crises can persist or deteriorate further if additional contagion events emerge.
Snapshot availability and later revisions are caller-attested, not independently verified.
